source.text:
09-CRO / testing and experiments

Goes here. Gathering qualitative and quantitative behavioral data to formulate test hypotheses. Heatmaps, session recordings, area maps, user testing platforms, and on-site surveys.

Not here.

Setting up custom event funnels and path explorations in Google Analytics 4 -> 06-MEA

Redesigning the landing page UI or changing copywriting based on the data -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the exact mechanics of Microsoft Clarity, explaining how to interpret rage clicks, dead clicks, excessive scrolling, and quick backs, and how to use Area Maps to design conversion rate tests. modules: [CRO] topics: [test design, session recordings, heatmaps] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. heatmaps / using Area Maps to see the exact percentage of clicks diverted to different page elements (e.g., specific navigation items, sticky filters, or non-clickable images). Analyzing scroll depth checkpoints (75%, 50%, 25%) to identify massive drop-offs caused by large text blocks or misplaced CTAs. Differentiating between the behaviors of cold traffic (needing social proof above the fold) and warm traffic. session recordings / isolating user frustration by filtering recordings for "rage clicks" (repeatedly clicking a non-clickable element or trying to close an immediate popup), "dead clicks" (clicking elements that look like links but aren't, such as "As Seen On" logos), "excessive scrolling" (skimming past long text blocks or frantically searching for a missing CTA), and "quick backs" (bouncing immediately from a product page because expected information is missing). Sort filtering by highest clicks to lowest, and lowest clicks to highest, to compare highly engaged users against unengaged users. test design / forming hypotheses based on behavioral data. For example, identifying that a "Contact Us" header takes up too much real estate, causing 25% of B2B users to drop off before seeing the actual form below the fold, and testing a layout where the form is moved up.

Look for. The definition of "rage clicks": rapidly clicking an element to exit an experience, such as a 5-second popup. The definition of "quick backs": navigating to a page and immediately returning, indicating the expected information was missing. The specific filtering method for recordings: sorting by Clicks High-to-Low and Pages High-to-Low, then comparing against the inverse (Low-to-High) to understand engaged vs. unengaged behavior. The rule for stopping recording review: stop watching once the main pattern of friction is identified, whether that takes 100 or 400 recordings. The 60% rule: acknowledging that statistically, 60% of people will never scroll past the hero section, meaning value props and social proof must be established in the first 5 seconds.

Skip. General promotion for the agency's audit services. Basic definitions of what e-commerce or B2B means.

Scope mix. Almost all baseline.

Volume. 10 to 15.
